subject: Post-demo: service venue narrowing, migration constraints & procurement next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia@novamed.com>, infra-eng@novamed.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo: service venue narrowing, migration constraints & procurement next steps

Hi Lydia / NovaMed infra team —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on requirements and velocity: 

Key constraints you told us during the call:
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 150ms for chat generation (current SLA target).
- Steady throughput: ~250 qps for inference bursts, with occasional spikes to 600 qps during batch processing windows.
- Data residency / HIPAA: logs must be retained in your VPC region, and egress must not route through third-party analytics.
- Migration source: you currently run a legacy GPU cluster (custom GPT-J variant) and some traffic is proxied via the OpenAI API gateway for new features.

Initial hosting fit thoughts (high-level):
- Redwood Dedicated: strong fit for predictable throughput and the burst+steady profile; gives reserved GPU pools and autoscale policies.
- Private VPC: may be required if procurement/legal insist on customer-managed networking and KMS integration for PHI.
- Hosted API: fastest path to production but requires a careful review of egress & data flow for PHI.

Migration considerations we discussed:
- Tokenizer parity and KV-cache keying for your custom GPT-J variant — we'll need a short tech spike to validate tokenization mapping and prefix cache behavior.
- Gradual cutover plan: proxy-based split traffic, then lift-and-shift of heavy-batch workloads.

Proposed next steps:
1) I will attach a short tech matrix and a draft SOW covering a 4-week validation spike (attachment).
2) Can infra share the existing GPU cluster manifest + sample model artifacts (S3 path or secured share) so our infra team can pre-validate quantization paths?
3) Procurement: what is your PO timeline? You mentioned an upcoming vendor window in ~45–60 days — please confirm.

If you prefer, we can propose two routes: (A) Dedicated + SOC2 evidence exchange (fast start) or (B) Private VPC pilot (longer legal lead time, full control). Recommend (A) to hit your 60-day window unless security needs force (B).

Attachments: SOW-draft.pdf, tech-matrix.xlsx

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198
[Attachment: SOW-draft.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]
[Attachment: tech-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 78KB)]
From: Lydia Park <lydia@novamed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-eng@novamed.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 17:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: service venue narrowing, migration constraints & procurement next steps

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments; helpful. A few clarifications from infra and procurement perspective: 

- Procurement: vendor window is likely 45 days, maybe up to 75 if we need extra security review. We can commit to a PO if the initial spike scope is limited to a fixed-fee validation and no production data is used.
- Security: SOC2 evidence is required; we will share the initial questionnaire tomorrow. Private VPC is preferred if we cannot get an acceptable egress control with hosted.
- Migration artifacts: infra will share a sanitized model artifact (tokenizer + sample weight manifest) via secure share by Friday. We cannot share full weights until NDA+procurement clears.

A couple of technical asks for your spike: 
1) Can Redwood run a tokenizer parity check with sample inputs we will provide?
2) For the Dedicated route: what is the minimum reserved capacity you recommend to meet the 250 qps baseline and the specified burst profile?

If you can answer those two items quickly, we can decide whether to start with Dedicated (faster) vs. go full Private VPC (parallel legal work).

Regards,
Lydia Park
Head of ML Ops | NovaMed
lydia@novamed.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: service venue narrowing, migration constraints & procurement next steps

Marissa / Karthik — FYI and asking for quick input so we can respond to Lydia. Thread below.

Key asks to answer in our reply:
- Tokenizer parity spike: estimate effort (engineer-days + infra) and whether we can re-use existing quantization tests. Suggest 3–5 engineer-days for prototype + 2 small GPU nodes for 48 hours.
- Dedicated minimum reservation to hit 250 qps baseline: Karthik, can you provide a conservative capacity recommendation (GPUs / vram / model sharding)? Also note they may require burst to 600 qps for short windows.
- Legal/security: we should attach our SOC2 bundle and call out the Private VPC lead time (estimate 6–8 weeks from signed order for network setup + KMS).

I think the right play: offer a fixed-fee 3-week validation spike on Dedicated config (limited data) to fit their 45–60 day PO window; run security questionnaire in parallel and surface Private VPC as Plan B. Marissa, want your sign-off on commercial carve (discount / pilot credits) to make the PO easier.

Thanks —
Ben

[Quoted message included below]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia@novamed.com>, infra-eng@novamed.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 18:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: service venue narrowing, migration constraints & procurement next steps

Lydia —

Appreciate the quick reply and the timelines. Below are concrete next steps and what we will deliver this week to keep momentum: 

Deliverables this week (Redwood):
- Short tech plan + resource estimate for a tokenizer parity spike and cache-behavior check (attached SOC2 bundle for your review).
- Recommended Dedicated reservation for baseline and burst (conservative numbers + autoscale path).
- Draft fixed-fee validation SOW with milestones and acceptance criteria (see attached SOW-draft.pdf).

What we need from NovaMed (by Friday):
- Sanitized tokenizer + small artifact bundle for parity tests (S3 or secure share).
- Confirmation on PO window (45 vs 75 days) so we can size commercial carve.
- Initial security questionnaire answers so we can pre-fill and speed legal review.

Notes on migration approach (brief):
- Strategy: proxy-split traffic -> validation on Dedicated nodes -> cutover of batch traffic -> optional Private VPC handoff.
- Risk: tokenizer mismatch and prefix-KV cache semantics are the biggest unknowns. If parity fails we will propose a thin adapter layer during cutover to translate keys.

If this plan looks good I will schedule a 30-minute technical sync (Redwood infra eng + NovaMed infra) for Friday to walk the artifact share and test plan.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2-evidence.zip (ZIP, 3.2MB)]
